## JSP-000005 · Existence and smoothness of the 3D Navier–Stokes equations

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Date proposed | 2000 (Millennium Prize formulation); equations originated in 1822/1845 |
| Mathematical area | Partial differential equations / Fluid mathematics |
| Problem description | For three-dimensional incompressible viscous flow, do smooth initial data always yield globally smooth solutions, or can finite-time singularities be constructed under the official conditions? |
| Current status | Solved<br>Proof contributors: OpenAI team. |
| Lean proof | Yes — [Lean source: option D](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/ComparatorTheorem.lean); [Lean source: option C](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/NavierStokes/ComparatorR3Theorem.lean)<br>Formalization contributors: @openai. |
| Attribution basis | Institutional credit; individual human contributors are not separately named. [Solver attribution source 1](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/README.md) [Lean attribution source 1](https://github.com/openai/NavierStokesAndEuler/blob/f9e8bc5b38b6e212696e8a30e3e91517af887bbd/README.md) |
| Eligible to claim | Yes |
| Historical bounty | USD 1,000,000<br> Source: <https://www.claymath.org/millennium/navier-stokes-equation/> |
| Elapsed years | About 26 years (since 2000) |
| Publication details | [P1] [Finite time blowup for Navier–Stokes](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/32d9f210-8b73-45e0-91bc-82a30aef8a9a/navier-stokes.pdf) (2026-09-08), announced proof of options C and D. [Announcement](https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/). Independent review remains pending. |
| Scholarly recognition | An official OpenAI solution announcement and public Lean formalization exist. The publisher's claim is not independent peer review or general mathematical acceptance; this review did not confirm those processes were complete. Clay currently labels the problem Active. Announcement: <https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/>; Clay: <https://www.claymath.org/millennium/navier-stokes-equation/> |

## JSP-000007 · Poincaré conjecture

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Date proposed | 1904 |
| Mathematical area | Geometric topology / Geometric analysis |
| Problem description | Is every closed simply connected three-manifold homeomorphic to the three-sphere? |
| Current status | Solved<br>Proof contributors: Grigori (Grisha) Perelman (solution; papers [P1–P3]). |
| Lean proof | No |
| Eligible to claim | No |
| Historical bounty | USD 1,000,000 (awarded in 2010; declined by Perelman)<br> Source: <https://www.claymath.org/millennium/poincare-conjecture/> |
| Elapsed years | About 98 years (since 1904) |
| Independent verification | Independent mathematical expositions: Bruce Kleiner and John Lott, [Notes on Perelman's papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605667); John Morgan and Gang Tian, [Ricci Flow and the Poincare Conjecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607607). These are mathematical verification accounts, not Lean formalizations.  |
| Publication details | [P1] [The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211159) (2002); [P2] [Ricci flow with surgery on three-manifolds](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0303109) (2003); [P3] [Finite extinction time for the solutions to the Ricci flow on certain three-manifolds](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307245) (2003). All three were released as preprints. |
| Scholarly recognition | Unverified: no public recognition specifically identifying this result was found (such as an award citation or authoritative public confirmation). |
